response.reason: The cited clause (Art. 26(2)(a) of Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011) establishes that the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance is mandatory if omitting it could mislead consumers about the true origin of the food, especially if the labeling might otherwise suggest a different origin. The verdict turns on this requirement, stating that the origin is declared and matches for both the product and its primary ingredient, thus satisfying the obligation set out in the cited clause. The clause is directly relevant to the requirement being assessed.
